approach.text: Bid compliance: assemble the tender as one PDF of no more than 20 pages and submit it via the portal by 2026-12-01 12:00 UTC, ensuring the service is live for students by 2027-01-11.
approach.basis: The deadline and page limit are set by the procurement process, and the live date aligns with the start of spring enrollment.

approach.text: Service features: provide signing capabilities for all current desktop and mobile browsers, and integrate with the student records system using the existing REST API.
approach.basis: Browser compatibility is baseline for web services, and the use of the REST API is the stated method for student system integration.

approach.text: Signature management: log every signature event with user identity, time, and version while retaining all signed documents for ten years and sending reminders after 72 hours of inactivity.
approach.basis: Automated logs and retention satisfy the record-keeping standards required for digital signing.

approach.text: Operational excellence: maintain 99.5% service availability each month, with planned maintenance notified five working days before execution.
approach.basis: The service availability and maintenance notification period ensure minimal disruption to user access.

risks.condition: The College plans to replace its student records system during 2027 (SRC-0012), but the bid assumes integration with the current system's REST API (SRC-0027) must be functional by 2027-01-11.
risks.event: The College implements a new records system mid-contract, causing the API integration to break and preventing identity or document verification.
risks.effect: Disruption of enrollment signing processes and inability for the platform to verify student data, leading to a service outage.
assumptions: The current REST API will remain stable until the replacement occurs.
The College will provide sufficient lead time for integration rework.
risks.trigger: The College announces the procurement or go-live timeline for the new student records system.
responses: Draft a change management clause requiring the College to provide technical API specifications for the new system at least 90 days prior to switchover.
Architect the integration layer as an abstraction to isolate the signing service from the specific records system API.
risks.residual_exposure: Reliance on the College's communication regarding their infrastructure roadmap.

risks.condition: The service must be live on 2027-01-11 (SRC-0032), but the migration of existing signed records is not required until 2027-02-28 (SRC-0026), a gap of 48 days.
risks.event: Users access the new service during the spring enrollment period but find historical documents are not present, appearing as missing.
risks.effect: High volume of support tickets regarding missing documentation, resulting in administrative overhead and a loss of user confidence in the platform.
assumptions: Students do not strictly require historical records for spring enrollment tasks.
The old system remains accessible for read-only lookups during this gap.
risks.trigger: Helpdesk receives requests regarding missing records after 2027-01-11.
responses: Prioritize the migration of documents from the last 12 months for completion before 2027-01-11.
Display a message in the new UI directing users to the legacy system for records created prior to 2027-01-11.
risks.residual_exposure: 48 days of degraded user experience regarding historical record retrieval.

domain_brief.summary: Higher education e-signature procurement requires technical integration with academic identity federations (InCommon, Shibboleth, SAML 2.0) and rigorous adherence to FERPA regulations for data governance. Bidders must navigate the consolidated HECVAT 4 assessment framework, replacing older standalone questionnaires and the retired Community Broker Index. Architecturally, institutions require webhook-driven event processing for real-time synchronization with SIS/ERP systems, prioritizing idempotent middleware to handle events asynchronously without violating API rate limits or creating data duplicates.

items.statement: Systems must uphold 34 CFR § 99.30 (FERPA) by enforcing the 'school official exception,' ensuring data is used exclusively for contract fulfillment and prohibiting secondary data mining or model training.

needs.need: FERPA-aware attribute release controls that filter PII for students with active disclosure blocks.
